problems.title: Using a value that may be missing
problems.scenario: find_user(id) returns a user only when id is 1. The program calls it with 2 and reads the length of the user's name without checking.
problems.best: The compiler refuses to read from a value that may be missing.

problems.title: Adding past the largest 64-bit integer
problems.scenario: The program reads the largest 64-bit integer from the command line and adds 1.
problems.best: The exact sum, or an overflow error. Wrapping around to a negative number is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Dividing an integer by zero
problems.scenario: The program divides 100 by a number it reads at run time: 0.
problems.best: A clear error. Infinity, NaN or a hardware crash fails.

problems.title: Shifting past the integer's width
problems.scenario: The program shifts 1 left by a count it reads at run time (64), using the language's 64-bit integer.
problems.best: The exact value 2^64, or an error. Getting 1 or 0 back is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Squeezing 300 into a byte
problems.scenario: The program converts 300, read at run time, to an unsigned 8-bit number with the language's standard conversion.
problems.best: An error, because 300 does not fit in 8 bits. Printing 44 silently drops the high bits.

problems.title: Converting 1e20 to a 64-bit integer (CERT FLP34-C)
problems.scenario: The program reads 1e20 from the command line as a 64-bit float, converts it to a 64-bit integer with the language's standard conversion, and prints it.
problems.best: An error, because 1e20 does not fit in 64 bits, or the exact 100000000000000000000 where integers have no fixed size. A clamped or wrapped number is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Comparing a negative index with a length
problems.scenario: The program checks whether i = -1 is less than the length of a 3-item list.
problems.best: "less", or the compiler refuses to compare a signed and an unsigned number. C converts -1 to a huge unsigned number and says no.

problems.title: Passing text where a number is expected
problems.scenario: add(a, b) adds two integers. The program calls it with the command-line text "5" and the number 3.
problems.best: The compiler refuses the call. "53" or a silent 8 fails; a run-time type error earns half.

problems.title: A function that can end without a result
problems.scenario: grade(score) returns "pass" above 50 and "fail" below 50. For exactly 50 it reaches the end without returning anything.
problems.best: The compiler refuses a function that can end without a result. Returning nothing, undefined or garbage fails.

problems.title: A match that forgets a case
problems.scenario: Color is Red, Green or Blue. name(c) handles only Red and Green, and the program calls it with Blue.
problems.best: The compiler refuses the match because it misses Blue.

problems.title: Reading a variable before it has a value
problems.scenario: The program declares x without a value and sets it only when n > 5. n is 1, and the program prints x.
problems.best: The compiler refuses to read x before it is set. An implicit 0 or undefined is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Calling a function with too few arguments
problems.scenario: The program calls area(w, h) as area(3).
problems.best: The compiler refuses the call. Getting NaN from the missing argument fails.

problems.title: Setting a misspelled field
problems.scenario: Config has a field color that starts as "blue". The program sets cfg.colour = "red" and prints cfg.color.
problems.best: The compiler refuses, because colour does not exist. Quietly creating a new field and printing "blue" fails.

problems.title: Assigning inside an if
problems.scenario: x is 5. The program writes if (x = 1), meaning x == 1.
problems.best: "not one": the language refuses an assignment as a condition. Taking the branch fails.
problems.warn: assignment.*(condition|parenthes)|result of an assignment|found .= in conditional|assigned in condition|in conditional, should be ==

problems.title: A switch case without break
problems.scenario: n is 1. Case 1 sets name to "one" but has no break, and case 2 sets it to "two".
problems.best: "one": cases do not fall through, or the compiler refuses. Printing "two" fails.

problems.title: Treating zero as missing
problems.scenario: The program parses a quantity of 0 into an optional and tests it with if (qty).
problems.best: "have 0", or the compiler refuses to use an optional as a true/false value. Printing "missing" fails.

problems.title: Comparing built strings with ==
problems.scenario: The program builds s = "ab" + the command-line text "c" and compares s == "abc".
problems.best: "equal". Comparing object identity and printing "different" fails.

problems.title: Parsing "12abc" as a number
problems.scenario: The program parses "12abc" with the shortest standard call that returns an integer, then adds 1.
problems.best: An error, or a failure the program must handle. Getting 13, 1 or NaN fails.

problems.title: Putting a cat in a list of dogs
problems.scenario: The program treats a list of Dogs as a list of Animals, stores a Cat through it, then prints the sound of dogs[0].
problems.best: "woof": the compiler refuses the view, or the view is a copy. A store-time run-time error earns half; "meow" from the dog list fails.

problems.title: Removing items while looping over them
problems.scenario: The program loops over [1, 2, 2, 3] and removes each 2 from the list as it goes, then prints the list.
problems.best: "1,3", a modification error, or a refusal. Skipping the second 2 fails.

problems.title: Locking a mutex twice
problems.scenario: The program locks a mutex, then calls a helper that locks the same mutex.
problems.best: "done" because the lock is re-entrant, or a deadlock error. Hanging forever fails.

problems.title: Closures made in a loop
problems.scenario: The program makes one closure in each pass of a loop over i = 0, 1, 2. Each closure returns i. It calls all three.

problems.title: Taking a snapshot by assignment
problems.scenario: The program saves before = weights, sets weights[1] = 5 and weights[3] = 0, then counts the positions where before differs.
problems.best: 2. If assignment shares the list instead of copying it, the program sees 0 changes.

problems.title: Ignoring a failed save
problems.scenario: save(path) writes a file and reports failure the language's usual way. The program calls it with /nonexistent/dir/out.txt, ignores the result and prints "saved".
problems.best: The compiler refuses to let the error go unhandled. Stopping with an exception earns half; printing "saved" fails.
problems.warn: unused .*(Result|result|return)|must be used|nodiscard|warn_unused|ignor(ed|ing) (the )?(error|result|return)|return value .*(ignored|unused)|unchecked error|errcheck|failed to open stream

problems.title: Sorting numbers that include NaN
problems.scenario: The program sorts [5, NaN, 3, 1, NaN, 4, 2] with the default sort and checks whether the real numbers came out in order.
problems.best: "ordered", or the compiler refuses to sort floats without a total order. A scrambled result fails.

problems.title: Dividing integers into a float
problems.scenario: sum = 7 and count = 2 are integers. The program sets a float avg = sum / count and prints it with one decimal.
problems.best: 3.5, or the compiler refuses the silent integer-to-float step. 3.0 fails.
problems.warn: integer division|implicit conversion from '?int|int.* to .*(float|double)|division of integers

problems.title: A number written with a leading zero
problems.scenario: The program writes a zip code as the literal 01234 and prints it.
problems.best: 1234, or the compiler refuses the literal. Reading it as octal and printing 668 fails.

problems.title: A list as a default argument
problems.scenario: add_item(item, cart = an empty list) adds the item to the cart and returns it. The program calls it twice without a cart and prints the second cart's length.
problems.best: 1: each call gets a fresh list. 2 means both calls share one list.

problems.title: Using a lazy sequence twice
problems.scenario: evens is a lazy filter of the numbers 1 to 6. The program sums evens, then counts evens, and prints both.
problems.best: "12 3", or the compiler refuses the second use. "12 0" fails; an error earns half.

problems.title: Bitwise and next to ==
problems.scenario: x is 4, from the command line. The program tests evenness with x & 1 == 0, without parentheses.
problems.best: "even", or the compiler refuses. Reading it as x & (1 == 0) and printing "odd" fails.

problems.title: An else meant for the outer if
problems.scenario: a is false and b is true. The program writes if a then (if b then r = "both") else r = "not a", without braces where the language allows it.
problems.best: "not a": blocks are explicit, or the compiler refuses. Attaching the else to the inner if leaves r unset.
problems.warn: dangling|ambiguous .*else|misleading indent|else|should be enclosed in a block

problems.title: Writing 1 < x < 3
problems.scenario: x is 5, from the command line. The program tests the range with 1 < x < 3.
problems.best: "outside": the language reads it as math does, or refuses it. Reading it as (1 < x) < 3, which is true, fails.

problems.title: Updating a copy inside a loop
problems.scenario: accounts holds one Account with balance 100, in the language's default record type. The program adds 50 to each account's balance in a for-each loop, then prints accounts[0].balance.
problems.best: 150, or the compiler refuses because the loop variable is read-only. Updating a copy and printing 100 fails.

problems.title: User text in a shell command (CWE-78)
problems.scenario: The program runs echo with a message from the command line: "hi; touch /tmp/bb_pwned". It uses the standard library's call that takes the whole command as one string, or its argument-list call if it has no one-string form. Then it reports whether /tmp/bb_pwned exists.
problems.best: "safe": the message reaches echo as an argument. A call that hands the string to a shell runs the injected command and fails.

problems.title: Comparing floats with == (CWE-1077)
problems.scenario: x = 0.1 and y = 0.2 come from the command line. The program compares x + y == 0.3.
problems.best: "equal" through exact decimals, or the compiler refuses. Binary floats print "not equal"; a compiler warning earns a bonus.

problems.title: Two locks taken in opposite orders (CWE-833)
problems.scenario: Two workers lock A and B in opposite orders. A rendezvous waits until both workers hold their first lock before each attempts the second.
problems.best: The program detects the lock-order deadlock or hangs. A deterministic rendezvous ensures the conflicting lock attempts occur.

problems.title: Joining a folder with an absolute path (CWE-22)
problems.scenario: The program joins /srv/app/uploads with a file name from the command line, /etc/passwd, using the standard path join, and checks that the result is still inside /srv/app/uploads.
problems.best: "inside", or an error. A join that drops the folder and returns /etc/passwd fails.

problems.title: A regex that backtracks forever (CWE-1333)
problems.scenario: The program matches the standard regex ^(a+)+$ against 40 a's followed by "!", read from the command line.
problems.best: "no match" quickly, from an engine that runs in linear time, or a clean limit error. Running for minutes fails.

problems.title: Testing a negative number for oddness (CERT INT10-C)
problems.scenario: is_odd(n) is n % 2 == 1. The program calls it with -3 from the command line.
problems.best: "odd". Where % keeps the sign, -3 % 2 is -1 and the test wrongly says "even".

problems.title: A missing comma in a list of strings
problems.scenario: The program lists three names, one per line, with no comma after the second, and prints the list's length.
problems.best: 3, or the compiler refuses. Gluing the two strings together and printing 2 fails.

problems.title: Returning from a cleanup block (CWE-584)
problems.scenario: save_report() writes a report, and the write fails. Its cleanup block (finally, ensure, defer) returns a status. The caller prints "failed" if save_report reports the failure, else "saved".
problems.best: "failed", or the compiler refuses. A return in the cleanup block swallows the error and prints "saved".

problems.title: return with its value on the next line
problems.scenario: total(a, b) has return on one line and a + b on the next. The program prints total(2, 3).
problems.best: 5, or the compiler refuses. Where the line break ends the statement, the function returns nothing.
problems.warn: unreachable|not reached|never (be )?executed|dead code|treated as an argument|newline

problems.title: A worker's failure lost between threads (CWE-248)
problems.scenario: A worker thread sums the numbers on the command line: "1 2 x 4". Parsing "x" fails the language's usual way (an exception, a panic or an error). The main thread waits for the worker with the basic thread or task call and prints the total.
problems.best: The failure reaches the main thread: the program stops with the error, or prints "failed". Printing a total and exiting normally fails.

problems.title: Starting a save and never waiting for it
problems.scenario: save() waits 50 ms, then records one item. The program starts it with the language's asynchronous call (async/await where the language has it, otherwise a thread or task), forgets to wait, and prints how many items are recorded.
problems.best: 1, or the compiler refuses. A task nobody waits for leaves the count at 0.
problems.warn: await|join|unused|never used|must be used|never read|implicitly ignored

problems.title: A format string missing an argument (CWE-685)
problems.scenario: The program builds "<done> of <total>" with the language's template-and-arguments formatting call but passes only the first value. A language with only string interpolation writes the interpolated string.
problems.best: The compiler refuses, or "3 of 5" where the mistake cannot be written. A run-time format error earns half; printing a placeholder or garbage fails.

problems.title: Subtracting below zero in an unsigned length (CERT INT30-C)
problems.scenario: HEADER is 5 and the command-line message is "abc". The program computes payload = length(message) - HEADER in the type the language's length call returns, and prints "short" if payload < 0, else payload.
problems.best: "short": the length is signed, or the subtraction is refused or stops at run time. Wrapping around to a huge payload fails.

problems.title: Reading a key the map does not have
problems.scenario: stock is the language's hash map {apple: 3, plum: 4}. The program reads stock["pear"] with the map's ordinary lookup (its index form where it has one) and prints it plus 5. Where the lookup returns an optional the language makes the caller check, the missing case prints "unknown".
problems.best: A refusal, a missing-key error, or "unknown". Printing 5, NaN or a default fails.

problems.title: Changing a key after putting it in a set
problems.scenario: seen is the language's hash set of integer lists, in its default list type (a hash map where there is no set). The program adds key = [1, 2] to seen, then sets key[0] = 9. For each item in seen it prints "found" if seen contains it, else "lost".
problems.best: "found": the set keeps its own copy or compares by identity, or a list cannot be a key at all. "lost" means the set holds an item it can no longer find.

problems.title: Declaring a new variable instead of assigning
problems.scenario: status starts as "pending". When the command-line flag is "ok", the code means to set status to "done" but declares a new status inside the if block (with let, var, := or a type name) and logs it. After the block it prints status.
problems.best: The compiler refuses the redeclaration, or "done" where a block cannot declare a new variable. Printing "pending" fails.
problems.warn: shadow|redefin|already (defined|declared)|hid(es|ing)|conceal|does not need to be mutable|unset local variable|never (re)?assigned

problems.title: Ignoring the new value a method returns
problems.scenario: name is "ada". The program calls the language's uppercase operation on name as a statement, ignores the result, and prints name.
problems.best: The compiler refuses to drop the result, or "ADA" where the call changes the string in place. Printing "ada" fails.
problems.warn: unused|must be used|ignored|discard|no effect|not used|pure expression|value of type|does not use

problems.title: Reading the item before the first
problems.scenario: readings is [10, 20, 30]. The program reads a position from the command line (0) and prints readings[i] - readings[i - 1]. The first reading has nothing before it.
problems.best: An index error. Reading the last item through -1, or a missing value, fails.

problems.title: Sorting numbers with the default sort
problems.scenario: The program sorts the integers [10, 9, 1] with the default sort and prints them.
problems.best: "1 9 10". Sorting them as text and printing "1 10 9" fails.

problems.title: Looking up a value of the wrong type (CWE-1024)
problems.scenario: ids is the integer list [10, 20, 30]. The program passes the command-line text "20", unparsed, to the list's standard membership test and prints "found" or "missing".
problems.best: The compiler refuses to compare text with integers. Printing "missing" fails.
problems.warn: unrelated|incompatible|never (be )?equal|always (false|true)|unlikely (argument|type)|type mismatch|not of type|inferred to be union type

problems.title: Writing to a closed file (CWE-910)
problems.scenario: The program opens /tmp/bb_close.txt, writes "a", closes it the language's usual way, then writes "b" with the language's usual error handling and prints "ok".
problems.best: The compiler refuses the write. A run-time error earns half; printing "ok" fails.

problems.title: Computing a value and printing the wrong one (CWE-563)
problems.scenario: price is 40, from the command line. The program computes total = price + 2 but prints price.
problems.best: The compiler refuses the unused total. A warning earns a bonus; printing 40 fails.
problems.warn: unused|never (used|read)|not used|assigned but|but never|declared and not used|no effect|isn't used|is never used

problems.title: Failing in the middle of a locked update (CWE-460)
problems.scenario: A ledger's debits and credits must stay equal. The language's standard tool for shared state guards them: a mutex, or a cell that holds the lock and the value together (an MVar, an atom). A worker takes the lock, adds 50 to debits, then fails the same way as in worker_failure_lost (an exception, a panic or an error) before it adds 50 to credits. The main thread waits for the worker, notes any failure the thread call reports, takes the lock and prints "balanced" or "unbalanced".
problems.best: "balanced" because the update never lands, or the program stops: the failure ends the process, or the lock reports that its holder failed. Printing "unbalanced" reads a half-done update.

problems.title: Cutting a string in the middle of a character (CWE-135)
problems.scenario: name is "a👍b". The program keeps the first n characters of name, with n = 2 read from the command line, using the language's usual slice or substring call, and prints them.
problems.best: a👍, or an error. Half a character, a replacement mark or a question mark is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Writing past the end of a buffer
problems.scenario: A 4-slot buffer sits next to guard = 7. The program writes 99 to slot 4, read from the command line, then prints the guard.
problems.best: A bounds error, or a guard that is still 7. A guard of 99 means memory was overwritten.
problems.warn: out of bounds|array index|past the end|beyond|undefined (array )?(key|offset)|index .* out of range

problems.title: Reading past the end of a buffer (CWE-125)
problems.scenario: A 4-slot buffer holding 1, 2, 3 and 4 sits next to secret = 42. The program reads slot 4, taken from the command line, and prints it.
problems.best: A bounds error. Printing 42 means the program read memory it does not own; printing a placeholder such as nil or undefined is a silent wrong answer.
problems.warn: out of bounds|array index|past the end|beyond|undefined (array )?(key|offset)|index .* out of range

problems.title: Using a record after freeing it
problems.scenario: The program creates a record holding 1234, keeps a second handle to it, frees it the normal way, creates 16 records holding 6666, and reads through the old handle.
problems.best: 1234, because the handle keeps the record alive, or the compiler refuses. 6666 or garbage means freed memory was reused.

problems.title: Freeing a record twice
problems.scenario: The program frees the same record twice, creates two records holding 1 and 2, and prints the first.
problems.best: 1: freeing twice is harmless or impossible, or the compiler refuses. An allocator abort is a crash; two records sharing memory is corruption.

problems.title: Returning a reference to a local
problems.scenario: make() returns a reference to its local 4242. clobber() writes its own locals. The program prints through the reference.
problems.best: 4242, because the value moves to the heap, or the compiler refuses.

problems.title: Keeping a reference into a growing list
problems.scenario: The program takes a reference to v[0], adds 1,000 items to v so it moves, creates w = [7], writes 99 through the old reference, and prints w[0].
problems.best: 7, or the compiler refuses. 99 means the write landed in memory that now belongs to w.

problems.title: Reading a fresh buffer's old contents
problems.scenario: The program writes SECRET-TOKEN into a 64-byte buffer at offset 32, frees it, creates a new 64-byte buffer and prints bytes 32 to 44 in hex.
problems.best: Zeros. Seeing SECRET-TOKEN again leaks data.

problems.title: Recursing 100 million levels deep
problems.scenario: walk(n) = (walk(n - 1) * 31 + n) mod 1000000007, and walk(0) = 0. The program calls walk(100,000,000). The formula keeps optimizers from turning the recursion into a loop.
problems.best: The answer, 919423987, or a stack-overflow error. A segmentation fault fails.

problems.title: Eight threads writing one map without a lock
problems.scenario: 8 threads each add 100,000 different keys to one shared map with no lock. The program prints the map's size.
problems.best: 800000, a detected concurrent-write error, or a refusal. A wrong size or a crash means the map was corrupted.

problems.title: Allocating a size taken from user input
problems.scenario: The program reads n = 10^13 from the command line, allocates n zero bytes, sets the last one and prints the length.
problems.best: A clean allocation error. A segmentation fault or being killed for running out of memory fails.

problems.title: Opening files and never closing them
problems.scenario: With a limit of 512 open files, the program opens a file 5,000 times, reads one byte each time and lets the handle go out of scope without closing it.
problems.best: "done": handles close when they go out of scope. Running out of file handles is a leak.

problems.title: Reading a value as the wrong type
problems.scenario: A Value holds an integer or text and currently holds 42. The program reads it as text and prints the text's length.
problems.best: The compiler refuses, or a clean run-time type error. Reading the integer's bits as a pointer crashes or leaks memory.

problems.title: Using user input as a format string
problems.scenario: The program logs a message from the command line, %s%s%n{}{0}, by passing it as the format to the language's formatted print call. The message covers both printf-style and brace-style placeholders.
problems.best: The message printed as is, a refusal (the format must be a literal), or a clean error. Reading missing arguments off the stack fails.

problems.title: Freeing a long linked list
problems.scenario: The program builds a linked list of 1,000,000 nodes, each owning the next, then frees it the language's usual way (dropping it, freeing it in a loop, or leaving it to the collector) and prints "done".
problems.best: "done". This program has no bug; a runtime that frees the chain by recursion and overflows the stack fails.

problems.title: Changing a character in a string literal (CERT STR30-C)
problems.scenario: greeting is the string literal "hello". The program sets greeting[0] = 'j' with the language's index assignment and prints greeting.
problems.best: A refusal because strings are immutable, a run-time error, or "jello" where strings are mutable values. Writing into read-only memory fails.

problems.title: Two records that point at each other, then dropped
problems.scenario: Each pass of a loop makes a parent and a child, each holding 4 KB of data and a reference to the other: the language's default reference, or its standard shared pointer where references are not shared by default. The pass then drops both. The program makes 1,500,000 pairs in a container with 3 GB of memory and prints "done".
problems.best: "done": the runtime frees each pair once nothing outside points at it. Running out of memory shows each pair kept the other alive.

problems.title: Building a record without one of its fields
problems.scenario: Config has the fields timeout and retries, neither with a default. The program builds a Config with only the timeout and prints retries.
problems.best: A refusal to build a Config without retries. Printing 0 or a placeholder is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Adding meters to seconds
problems.scenario: Meters and Seconds each wrap a 64-bit float. The program adds a distance of 2 m to a time of 3 s by mistake and prints the sum.
problems.best: A refusal to add Meters to Seconds. Printing 5 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Passing an integer where an enum is expected
problems.scenario: Color is Red, Green or Blue, and name(c) returns a color's name. The program calls name with the integer 7 and prints the result.
problems.best: A refusal to pass 7 as a Color. Printing an empty name or a placeholder is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: An override that overrides nothing
problems.scenario: Circle means to replace Shape's describe() but misspells the method as descibe. The program prints describe() of a Circle.
problems.best: A refusal of a replacement method that matches nothing in Shape. Printing shape is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Forcing a missing value
problems.scenario: find(2) returns a missing value. The program prints before, then forces the value out with the language's shortest way to do so (*o, o!, o.get(), unwrap(), assert(o), or a null used as a number) and adds 1.
problems.best: The program stops there with an error. Printing a number, NaN or a placeholder is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A missing value printed as text
problems.scenario: find_name(id) returns a name only when id is 1, the same way find_user does in null_deref. The program calls it with 2 and prints a greeting with the name, using the language's string interpolation (or its usual formatting where it has none) without checking.
problems.best: A refusal to put a value that may be missing into text without saying what missing means. Printing hello, null, hello, None, hello, nil or hello, followed by nothing is a silent wrong answer that reaches users.

problems.title: A search that found nothing, used as a position
problems.scenario: line is user, read from the command line, with no colon in it. The program finds the position of : with the language's standard search call and prints the text after it, from that position plus 1, without checking that a colon was found.
problems.best: A refusal to use the search result as a position before checking it was found: the call answers an optional. A clear error at run time is next best. Printing user or ser treats "not found" (-1, false or nil) as a real position.

problems.title: The maximum of an empty list
problems.scenario: readings are the numbers given on the command line: none. The program takes their maximum with the language's standard call for the maximum of a list and prints it plus 1.
problems.best: A refusal to use the maximum as a number before checking the list had one: the call answers an optional. A clear error at run time is next best. Printing -Infinity, 1 or any other number treats an empty list as having a maximum.

problems.title: A function that changes the list it was given
problems.scenario: count(xs) should only read its list but sorts it in place. The program counts [3, 1, 2] and then prints the list's first item.
problems.best: 3, or a refusal to change a list the function only reads. Printing 1 means the caller's list changed under it.

problems.title: One account passed as both sides of a transfer
problems.scenario: transfer(from, to, amount) works out both new balances, then stores them. The program transfers 30 from an account to the same account, which should leave 100, and prints the balance.
problems.best: 100, or a refusal to pass one account as both arguments. 130 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Storing 300 in a byte
problems.scenario: The program stores the literal 300 in an 8-bit integer and prints it.
problems.best: A refusal, because 300 does not fit in 8 bits, or a clear error. Printing 44 silently drops the high bits.
problems.warn: overflow|out of range|does not fit|truncat|implicit conversion|changes value

problems.title: Passing a 64-bit integer as a 32-bit one
problems.scenario: n is a 64-bit integer holding 3,000,000,000, read at run time. The program passes it, without a conversion, to a function that takes a 32-bit integer and prints what it receives.
problems.best: 3000000000, or a refusal to narrow without a conversion. A negative number is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Sorting values that have no order
problems.scenario: Point has fields x and y and no defined order. The program sorts a list of Points and prints the first x.
problems.best: A refusal, or an error saying Points cannot be compared. Printing a point from an arbitrary order is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Passing 2^53 + 1 as a float (CERT FLP36-C)
problems.scenario: The program reads 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1) as a 64-bit integer and passes it, without a conversion, to a function that takes a 64-bit float and prints it as a whole number.
problems.best: 9007199254740993, or a refusal to convert implicitly. 9007199254740992 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A constant index past the end of an array
problems.scenario: table holds 3 entries. The program prints table[5], an index known to be out of range before the program runs.
problems.best: A refusal to build. A bounds error at run time is next best; printing a value or a placeholder is a silent wrong answer.
problems.warn: out of bounds|past the end|out of range|array index|array-bounds

problems.title: A running total that keeps every message alive
problems.scenario: The program reads 3,000,000 messages of 4 KB each from /dev/zero, 12 GB in all, in a container with 3 GB of memory. It adds each message's size to a running total kept in the language's standard mutable cell (a variable, or an IORef, ref or atom where values cannot change) with the cell's plain update, then drops the message. It prints the total.
problems.best: 12288000000: each message is freed once its size is added. Running out of memory shows the total kept every message alive until it was printed.

problems.title: A size that overflows before the allocation (CWE-680)
problems.scenario: A header says 2305843009213693953 (2^61 + 1) records of 8 bytes follow; the program reads the count at run time. It computes the buffer size as count * 8 in the language's 64-bit integer or size type, allocates a byte buffer of that size, sets the first byte of the second record (byte 8) to 99, and prints stored.
problems.best: A clear error at the multiplication, the allocation or the write. Printing stored shows the size wrapped to 8 bytes and the write went past the buffer.

problems.title: Constant arithmetic that overflows 64 bits
problems.scenario: The program computes the nanoseconds in 300 years, 1,000,000,000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 365 * 300, as a 64-bit constant and prints it.
problems.best: 9460800000000000000 where integers have no fixed size, or a refusal. A wrapped number is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Waiting for an answer from a worker that failed
problems.scenario: A worker parses x as an integer and sends the result back through the language's standard channel or queue. Parsing fails the language's usual way (an exception, a panic or an error) before anything is sent. The main thread waits for the answer with the channel's ordinary receive, with no timeout, and prints it.
problems.best: A clear error: the receive reports that nothing can arrive, or the worker's failure stops the program. Waiting forever is a hang in production.

problems.title: A blocking sleep inside asynchronous code
problems.scenario: Two jobs each wait 500 ms with the language's ordinary blocking sleep. The program runs both with the language's asynchronous call (async/await where the language and its standard library can run it, otherwise a thread, task or goroutine), waits for both, and prints concurrent if they finished within 800 ms, otherwise serial.
problems.best: concurrent, or a refusal of a blocking call inside asynchronous code. serial means one job's sleep stalled the other, as a blocking call stalls every request on an event loop.

problems.title: A statement after an early return (CWE-561)
problems.scenario: check() is meant to print ok and then checked, but a stray return sits between them, the shape of Apple's goto fail bug. The program calls check().
problems.best: A refusal of the code after the return. Printing only ok is a silent wrong answer.
problems.warn: unreachable|never be executed|dead code|not reachable|will never

problems.title: A misspelled name in string interpolation
problems.scenario: name is Ada. The program prints a greeting with string interpolation, but the placeholder misspells the variable as nmae.
problems.best: A refusal to build. A clear error at run time is next best; a greeting with an empty name is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Arguments with side effects (CERT EXP30-C)
problems.scenario: next() returns 1, then 2. The program prints pair(next(), next()).
problems.best: 1 2: the language runs a call's arguments left to right. 2 1 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A match arm that can never run
problems.scenario: describe(s) is meant to say circle for a circle and other for anything else, but the catch-all arm (or, where switch arms do not match in order, a repeated case) comes first. The program prints describe of a circle.
problems.best: A refusal of the arm that can never run. Printing other is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A repeated key in a map literal
problems.scenario: The program builds a map literal meant to hold the keys a and b, but types a twice, and prints the map's size.
problems.best: 2 cannot happen here, so the best outcome is a refusal; a clear error at run time is next best. Printing 1 means the second value silently replaced the first.

problems.title: A character used as a number
problems.scenario: c is the letter a. The program works out the next letter as c + 1 and prints it.
problems.best: b, or a refusal to add a number to a character without a conversion. Printing 98 or a1 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A comparison written instead of an assignment (CWE-482)
problems.scenario: count starts at 0. The program means to set it to 5 but writes count == 5, then prints count.
problems.best: A refusal of a comparison whose result is unused. Printing 0 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Comparing records with == (CWE-595)
problems.scenario: a and b are two records built separately, each with x = 1 and y = 2. The program compares them with == and prints equal or different.
problems.best: equal, or a refusal of == on records. different means == compared identity, not content.

problems.title: Equality without a matching hash (CWE-581)
problems.scenario: Point defines equality on x and y only, without a matching hash. The program puts two Points that are equal by that definition in a hash set and prints its size.
problems.best: 1, or a refusal of a key type whose hash can disagree with its equality. 2 means the set holds two equal values.

problems.title: A table with a missing entry
problems.scenario: table is meant to hold 4 entries but is written with 3 values. The program prints table[3].
problems.best: A refusal of a 4-entry table with 3 values, or a clear error. Printing 0 or a placeholder is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: Converting 7 to an enum with three values
problems.scenario: Color is Red, Green or Blue. The program prints before, then converts 7, read at run time, to a Color with the language's standard conversion and prints the result, or invalid if the conversion reports failure.
problems.best: invalid, or the program stops with an error. A Color that is none of the three is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: & where && was meant (CWE-768)
problems.scenario: s is empty. The program tests that s is not empty and starts with a, using & where && was meant, and prints yes or no.
problems.best: no, or a refusal of & between booleans. With & both sides run, so reading the first letter of an empty string may stop the program.

problems.title: Changing a field meant to be fixed
problems.scenario: Config has a port fixed when it is built. The program builds one with port 8080, then sets the port to 1 by mistake and prints it.
problems.best: A refusal to change the port. A clear error at run time is next best; printing 1 is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: An integer used as a condition
problems.scenario: compare(a, b) returns 0 when a equals b, as C's strcmp does. The program writes if (compare("x", "x")) meaning they are equal and prints same or different.
problems.best: same, or a refusal of an integer as a condition. Printing different is a silent wrong answer.

problems.title: A failed write lost when the file closes (CWE-252)
problems.scenario: The program writes the line data to /dev/full, a device where every write fails with no space left, using the language's usual file writer, closes it the usual way (the end of a block, defer, with or using, or a close call whose result it does not check) and prints saved.
problems.best: An error that stops the program. Printing saved means the data was lost with no sign, as when a disk fills up in production.
problems.warn: no space|space left|ENOSPC|bytes written|must be used|unchecked|result .*(unused|ignored)

problems.title: Using an explicitly null field as a value
problems.scenario: A decoded record is present, but its optional name field is explicitly null. The program reads the field as a string and prints its length without checking it.
problems.best: The compiler refuses the unchecked read, or the program stops with a clear null or missing-value error. Treating null as a valid name fails.

problems.title: A null check that a later call undoes
problems.scenario: session.user holds alice. The program checks that session.user is present, calls logout(session), which clears session.user, then prints the length of the user's name. Where the language checks an optional value by binding it to a name, the program binds it and reads the name from that binding.
problems.best: 5, from the user the check found, or a refusal to trust the check after a call that can change the field. Reading session.user again after logout reads a missing value.
problems.warn: smart cast|promot|possibly|may be null|might be null|could be null|can be null|CS8602|on null|null pointer|nullable|optional|\bnil\b|undefined

problems.title: An array of records with an empty slot
problems.scenario: Records arrive by position. Before any arrive, the program makes an array for 3 users the language's usual way to make an array it fills later. It stores users at positions 1 and 2, then prints the length of the name at position 0, which never arrived.
problems.best: A refusal to read a slot that may be empty, or a clear error. Printing 0, or garbage, treats the empty slot as a user.
problems.warn: possibly|may be null|might be null|could be null|can be null|CS8602|on null|null pointer|nullable|optional|\bnil\b|undefined|uninitiali

problems.title: A missing error passed on as a present one
problems.scenario: validate(name) returns the language's general error type. The name is valid, so the pointer to the specific ValidationError it holds is empty, and validate returns that pointer as the general error. The caller checks whether there is an error and prints valid or invalid.
problems.best: valid: an empty pointer stays empty as the general error type, or a refusal. invalid shows the general error counts as present while it holds an empty pointer.

problems.title: Checking and claiming a shared resource in separate steps
problems.scenario: Two workers each check under a lock whether one resource is unclaimed, release the lock, then claim it under a later lock. A barrier makes both checks happen before either claim.
problems.best: Exactly one worker claims the resource. Two successful claims show the check and update were not atomic.

problems.title: Changing a list after sending it to another thread
problems.scenario: The main thread sends the list [1, 2, 3] to a worker through the language's channel or queue, sets the first item of its own list to 99, then tells the worker to go on. The worker prints the first item of the list it received. Where the language's usual list cannot change, the program builds a new list with 99 first.
problems.best: 1: the worker got its own copy, or the compiler refuses the change because the list moved. 99 shows both threads hold one list.

problems.title: A wake-up sent before anyone waits
problems.scenario: The main thread sends a wake-up, then starts a worker that waits for it and prints "done", and waits for the worker to finish. The program uses the standard library's condition variable where it has one, and otherwise its standard way for one thread to wait for another (a channel, an MVar, a promise). The worker waits without first checking whether the wake-up already came.
problems.best: "done": the tool keeps a wake-up until someone takes it, or the program stops with a deadlock error. A condition variable drops a wake-up nobody waits for, so the worker waits forever.

problems.title: A balance checked before an await and spent after it
problems.scenario: balance is 100. withdraw(80) checks that the balance covers it, awaits a 10 ms fraud check, then subtracts. The program runs two withdrawals of 80 at once with the language's asynchronous call (async/await, fibers or go blocks run by the standard library's scheduler) and prints the balance. A language whose standard library has no asynchronous tasks cannot write this form; its threaded form is check_then_act.
problems.best: 20: one withdrawal goes through and the other is turned down, or a refusal to keep the check across the await. -60 shows both checks passed before either update.

problems.title: An early return that skips the unlock (CWE-667)
problems.scenario: withdraw(amount) locks the account's mutex, returns early when the balance is too low, and unlocks at its end. The program calls withdraw(500), which returns early, then starts a worker that calls withdraw(30), waits for the worker and prints the balance of 100. It locks and unlocks with the standard mutex's explicit calls; where the standard library offers only a lock released at the end of its scope, the early return cannot skip the release.
problems.best: 70: the lock is released on every way out of the function, or the program stops with a deadlock error. Waiting forever shows the early return kept the lock.
